gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2's solar input only accepts 12–28 V at up to 10 A and 200 W through an XT60 port, which rules out wiring panels in series. It also doesn't say that the station sold alone ships without a solar cable; BLUETTI's 10A MC4-to-XT60 cable for it costs $39.
standout_why: Compared against powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (read 2026-11-13). It has a station-by-station compatibility table, but the Elite 30 V2 isn't in it, and for the Jackery Explorer 300 v2 it says solar voltage and plug are 'Not listed'. Its general rule assumes 12–60 V stations. Also compared against offgridempire.com/best-solar-generator-under-500, which has no connector, voltage or cable data and only an 'Avoid If: 12V rigs' column. I couldn't open solargenadvisor.com/best-solar-generators-under-500 (SSL certificate error), so it isn't compared. Our own current row has 'BLUETTI: 2.2 h at its 200 W max' but no voltage ceiling and no cable note.
decides: This confirms the Elite 30 V2 + 100 W kit as the pick rather than changing it. The bundled 100 W panel works as shipped, and BLUETTI's US kit page shows 'free charging cable' in the 100 W bundle's image text. The finding adds two warnings. First, a shopper who later wants the full 200 W input can't put two 100 W panels in series, because about 2 × 22–25 V Voc is over 28 V. They need two panels in parallel or one 12 V-class 200 W panel with Voc of 28 V or less, and BLUETTI's 350 W and 500 W panels can't be used at all. Second, anyone who buys the $289.99 station alone and adds a separate panel has to add the $39 MC4-to-XT60 cable. That moves the parts-separately total on our page from $538.99 to $577.99, which widens the kit's advantage.
